sentences.text: The allegation against the petitioner is that during the year 2018, the accused and the defacto complainant were in a close relationship and the petitioner had sexual intercourse with the defacto complainant and impregnated her.
Later the pregnancy was aborted.
Subsequently, a complaint was submitted by the defacto complainant on 14.03.2023.
Thereafter, the petitioner was arrested on 16.03.2023 as part of the investigation.
Since then he has been under judicial detention.
This application is submitted seeking Regular Bail.
3. Heard Sri. S Rajeev, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri. M.P.Prasanth, learned Public Prosecutor for the State.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that BAIL APPL. NO.
3022 OF 2023 the petitioner is falsely implicated in the said case.
The learned counsel for the petitioner specifically highlights the huge delay in reporting the matter to the Police.
It is pointed out that the incident occurred in the year 2018, whereas the matter was reported to the Police only in the year 2023.

It is also pointed out that the defacto complainant is married subsequently and no plausible explanation is forthcoming from the part of the defacto complainant for the huge delay in reporting the matter to the Police.
4. On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor would oppose the aforesaid application.
It is pointed out that the matter is being investigated and the allegations raised against the petitioner are serious in nature, therefore dismissal of the application is essential.
5. I have gone through the records and heard the contentions raised from both sides.
After considering all the relevant aspects, I find some force in the contentions put forward by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
As rightly pointed out by him, the incident occurred in the year 2018 and subsequently the defacto complainant was married as BAIL APPL. NO. 3022 OF 2023 well.
The complaint was submitted only in the year 2023 and there is no proper explanation is seen made.
Now the petitioner is under judicial detention for more than one month.
There is substantial progress in the investigation.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find any necessity to continue the incarceration of the petitioner.

5. In the result, the application is allowed and the petitioner is directed to be released on bail subject to following conditions:-
i) The petitioner shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
ii) The petitioner shall fully co-operate with the investigation.
iii) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m on every Wednesday until the filing of final report.
iv) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.

2 v) The petitioner shall not commit any offence of like nature while on bail.

sentences.text: BAIL APPL. NO. 3022 OF 2023 vi) The petitioner shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
vii) The petitioner shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the jurisdictional court.
viii) The petitioner shall surrender his passport before the Jurisdictional court and, in case he does not have a passport, an affidavit to that effect shall be filed.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law.
